identity.description: The canonical count regression: models a non-negative integer target as Poisson-distributed with log-linear mean exp(x'B). Coefficients exponentiate to rate ratios; supports offsets/exposure for per-unit-time rates. Its defining commitment is equidispersion — variance EQUALS the mean.

consumes.note: target must be a non-negative integer count; optional offset/exposure column carried as a driver passthrough, not a port

emits.note: predicted mean count/rate lambda-hat; the fitted family defines a full count distribution P(Y=k|x) around it — no separate 'count' port exists, score is the closest match
log rate ratios with SEs/CIs; exp(B) is the multiplicative effect on the expected count

link.note: canonical log link almost always; identity/sqrt are statsmodels-supported alternates for special mean structures

alpha.note: fit_regularized elastic-net strength; 0.0 = plain IRLS MLE

invariances.why: unpenalized MLE is scale-equivariant, but the searchable elastic-net penalty (fit_regularized alpha) is NOT — penalized coefficient magnitudes depend on units, and badly-scaled columns condition the IRLS working matrix poorly
the linear predictor assumes log-linear covariate effects; a monotone transform of an input changes the fitted mean function
the IRLS likelihood has no missing-value mechanism — statsmodels raises or drops rows (missing='drop'), silently biasing the sample
the array API requires a pre-encoded design matrix; patsy formulas can encode but this driver takes matrices

assumes the conditional distribution is Poisson, whose single parameter forces variance = mean (equidispersion); overdispersed data keeps the mean estimate consistent but deflates SEs, fabricating significance
only p+1 parameters estimated by MLE; usable at tens-to-hundreds of rows with honest (wide) CIs
the log-linear form extends beyond the observed covariate range — predictions grow exponentially in x, so extrapolation is possible but aggressive

featureStats.why: the family's defining qualia stat: sample variance/mean of the count target — Poisson's likelihood forces this to 1, so a ratio well above 1 (overdispersion) is the gate toward NegativeBinomial before any fit is run

observed share of zeros vs the Poisson-implied exp(-lambda-hat); an excess-zero gap means zeros arrive from a second mechanism the single-parameter Poisson cannot express — the commit-zero-inflated signal
the Poisson likelihood is defined only on non-negative integers; negatives or non-integer values make the log-likelihood undefined — a reject-input check, not a modeling choice

modelMetrics.why: the post-fit dispersion estimate — approximately 1 under a correctly-specified Poisson; values well above 1 are the overdispersion red flag that re-routes to NB even when coefficients look significant
the GLM-native goodness-of-fit measure; deviance/df near 1 supports the distributional claim, letting the equidispersion assumption be checked rather than trusted

edgeCases.behavior: consistent mean but SEs too small — spurious significance
systematic underprediction of the zero class

edgeCases.condition: a covariate perfectly predicts zero counts

driver.constructor: sm.GLM(y, sm.add_constant(X), family=sm.families.Poisson(link=...), offset=..., exposure=...).fit(maxiter=..., tol=...) or .fit_regularized(alpha=..., L1_wt=...)
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant on the design matrix; predict returns the mean count; expose offset/exposure passthrough for rate models
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded IRLS fit; predict is thread-safe

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; statsmodels drops or rejects incomplete rows, biasing the fitted rates
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the log-linear fit the link assumes
unpenalized MLE is scale-equivariant, but standardization conditions IRLS and is required in practice whenever the searchable penalty alpha > 0
categoricals must be design-encoded before the likelihood sees the matrix
